# REST API: Auth

These routes of the platform API come from its [OpenAPI document](../openapi.json); [The REST API as a contract](../rest-api.md) says what Lakana promises about them.

## `POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/token`

Exchange a CI job's ID token for a Lakana token

Needs no credential: the ID token is the proof. The Lakana token acts as the service account of the one enabled CI trust rule whose conditions the ID token's claims match, for the environment and repository asked for. It may queue one deploy (of the ID token's commit only) or dry run there, then read that run, and it expires after the server's CI token lifetime (one hour by default). Answers 401 when the ID token is refused or was exchanged before, 403 when it is valid but no single enabled rule accepts it, 413 for a request over 16 KiB and 422 unless the body is a JSON object of `id_token`, `environment` and `repository` only.

Request body (application/json, required): object

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id_token` | text | yes |  |
| `environment` | text | yes |  |
| `repository` | text | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `CiTokenOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |

Answer fields: `CiTokenOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token` | text | yes |  |
| `expires_at` | text (date-time) | yes |  |
| `principal` | text | yes |  |
| `environment` | text | yes |  |
| `repository` | text | yes |  |
| `kinds` | list of text | yes |  |
| `sha` | text or null | yes |  |
| `rule_id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/token`

Exchange the one-time code of `lakana login` and its PKCE verifier for the new token

Needs no credential: the code and the verifier are the proof. The code is used up by the first exchange, right or wrong (400, the same sentence for an unknown, used, expired or wrong one, or when the browser session that confirmed it has ended). The token is the confirming person's, named `lakana login on <host>`, and works for 90 days. 429 past the rate.

Request body (application/json, required): `CliTokenIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | text | yes |  |
| `code_verifier` | text | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `TokenIssueOut` |
| `400` | The client closed the connection before the request body arrived in full. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `429` | Too many attempts from this address; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `TokenIssueOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key_id` | text | yes |  |
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `token` | text | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/device`

Start a sign-in of `lakana login --device`, for a computer without a browser

Needs no credential. Show `user_code` and `verification_url` to the person, who confirms in a browser where they are signed in; poll `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/device/token` every `interval` seconds. The codes work for 10 minutes. 429 past the rate.

Request body (application/json, required): `CliDeviceIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | text | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `CliDeviceOut` |
| `400` | The client closed the connection before the request body arrived in full. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `429` | Too many attempts from this address; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `CliDeviceOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device_code` | text | yes |  |
| `user_code` | text | yes |  |
| `verification_url` | text | yes |  |
| `expires_in` | whole number | yes |  |
| `interval` | whole number | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/device/token`

Ask whether a sign-in of `lakana login --device` was approved

Needs no credential: the device code is the proof. Answers ``pending`` until someone decides, then ``approved`` with the token once, or ``denied``; ``expired`` after 10 minutes and after the token was handed out. 429 with ``error: slow_down`` when asked again sooner than 5 seconds; 400 for an unknown device code.

Request body (application/json, required): `CliDevicePollIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device_code` | text | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `CliDevicePollOut` |
| `400` | The client closed the connection before the request body arrived in full. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `429` | Too many attempts from this address; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `CliDevicePollOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | one of `pending`, `approved`, `denied`, `expired` | yes |  |
| `token` | `TokenIssueOut` or null | yes |  |
